title: Jerome on 2 Chronicles 1:1
body: “The book of things omitted or epitome of the old dispensation is of such importance and value that without it any one who should claim to himself a knowledge of the scriptures would make himself a laughing stock in his own eyes.”
author: Jerome, Letter 53, to Paulinus

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Chronicles 6:42
body: “The word prosopolemptes--"respector of persons"--(personarum acceptor Vulg.) is a term founded upon the phrase, lambanein prhosopon, an imitation of the Hebrew ns' phnym, to accept the person, the presence; to have a favorable or partial regard to the outward appearance,--as opposed to hsyv phnym, to turn away the face (of the petitioner) i.e.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Acts and Romans

title: John Chrysostom on 2 Chronicles 34:14
body: “Where are these words written? Why, it is said to have been "written," then also, when it is set down, not in words, but in actual events, as in the historical books ; or when the same meaning is expressed, but not in the very same words, as in this place: for the words, "They to whom it was not told about Him shall see, and they who have not heard shall understand," (Is.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
